sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A slender Fijian tree of dense forest on Viti Levu, recorded from sea level to about 970 m and reaching around 10 m tall. Its very large compound leaves and light-brown hairs on young growth help distinguish it from the related A. parksii. The original botanical account describes sparse hairs near the base of the outer petals; the sources consulted do not verify the flower colour or mature fruit appearance shown in the plate.

sections.title: Uses and related species
sections.text: No food use is established in the sources consulted. A. evansensis is another Fijian Aglaia, but is documented in wet montane forest in north-western Viti Levu and has smaller leaves with three or five leaflets.

sources.title: Studies of Pacific Island Plants, X: The Meliaceae of Fiji, Samoa, and Tonga — Smithsonian
